answer: Price sybil resistance as a recurring toll, not a one-time bond. Every fresh identity pays a per-epoch path toll that decays only as it transacts with a widening set of distinct, established counterparts. The rebate curve is the mesa: its summit is velvet-smooth for agents whose interaction graph is broad, while the umber cliffs facing clone fleets stay steep - duplicates mostly trade with each other, so their diversity score never rises, tolls never rebate, and fleet cost grows linearly with its size while honest, well-connected agents pay almost nothing.
